The failing test `testJira567` calls the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method with arrays of mixed types. The test first tries to add an `Integer` array and a `Long` array, which is valid and should work correctly. Then, it tries to add an `Integer` array and a `Long` array again, but this time expects an `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown because you cannot store a `Long` in an `Integer` array.

The current bug report mentions that `ArrayUtils.addAll` does not handle mixed types very well. The description refers to an `ArrayStoreException` that occurs when attempting to add an `Integer` array to a `Long` array.

Looking at the code of `ArrayUtils.addAll`, we can see that it creates a new array and copies the elements of the input arrays into the new array. The method does not perform any type checking to ensure compatibility between the array types, leading to the `ArrayStoreException` when trying to store a `Long` in an `Integer` array.

To fix this issue, type checking should be added to ensure that elements being added to the new array are compatible with its component type.

Next, I will suggest the methods that need to be fixed to address this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.lang3.ArrayUtils.addAll(T[], T...)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
